VL53L4CD Laser Tripwire

  • VS Code
  • ESP32
  • ESP-IDF
  • C
  • FreeRTOS
  • I²C
  • WiFi
  • Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT)
  • Git
  • GitHub

Purpose and Function

Allow the user to wirelessly monitor sensor readings from anywhere in the world from any device as long as they have an internet connection.

This particular application utilizes a custom breakout board for the VL53L4CD sensor and the ESP32 microcontroller.

The user is able to monitor the sensor on their device and whether a person or object has passed through the IR laser emitted by the sensor.

Code and Logic

This project utilized and implemented ESP-IDF drivers for I²C, MQTT, WiFi, FreeRTOS, and the VL53L4CD sensor.

In particular it required understanding of FreeRTOS tasks and scheduling, WiFi Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP), MQTT topics, brokers, clients, and publishers, as well as I²C communication.

Result

The distance readings from this sensor are easily monitorable from a personal device such as a mobile phone, the ESP32 automatically connects to the specified local WiFi network and transmits these messages using MQTT.

Example code

An example code block that publishes MQTT messages to the topic: "sensors/vl53l4cd/distance_mm". See the GitHub repo for full code.

error_check = VL53L4CD_GetResult(dev, &result);

if (error_check == VL53L4CD_ERROR_NONE && result.range_status == 0) {

    //store distance measurements
    char payload[54];

    //Print distance to ESP-IDF terminal
    ESP_LOGI(TAG1, "Distance in mm: %" PRIu16 "\n", result.distance_mm);

    //Handles logic for distance readings sets motion_active and out_of_range flags
    handle_distance(result.distance_mm);

    //Publish MQTT messages
    if (motion_active && !out_of_range) {
        snprintf(payload, sizeof(payload), "Movement detected, Distance (mm): %u", result.distance_mm);
        esp_mqtt_client_publish(client, "sensors/vl53l4cd/distance_mm", payload, 0, 1, 0);
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1000));

    } else if(out_of_range) {
        //currently using max distance of 1200mm - can be increased
        snprintf(payload, sizeof(payload), "Out of Range");
        esp_mqtt_client_publish(client, "sensors/vl53l4cd/distance_mm", payload, 0, 1, 0);

    } else if (!out_of_range && no_change) {
        snprintf(payload, sizeof(payload), "No Movement detected, Distance (mm): %u", result.distance_mm);
        esp_mqtt_client_publish(client, "sensors/vl53l4cd/distance_mm", payload, 0, 1, 0);
    }
}
VL53L4CD_ClearInterrupt(dev);

VL53L4CD Time of Flight Breakout Board

  • KiCad
  • Circuit Design
  • I²C
  • SMD and THT Soldering
  • Low Dropout Regulators
  • Level Shifters

Purpose and Function

Create a breakout board for the VL53L4CD time of flight sensor that communicates distance measurements via I²C.

The board will include a LDO (Low-Dropout) regulator and level shifter for compatibility between the 2.8V and 3.3 or 5V microcontrollers.

Layout and Design

The goal of this design was to create a compact layout that allowed connectivity via header pins as well as JST connectors.

This PCB also features mounting holes so that it can be utilized in applications where the sensor must be stationary.

Result

A simple and compact breakout board for the VL53L4CD time of flight sensor that allows for accurate distance measurements and compatibility with both 5V and 3.3V logic level microcontrollers.

Sensorless Electronic Speed Controller (ESC) for Brushless DC Motor

  • STM32CubeIDE/MX
  • KiCad
  • Circuit Design
  • Brushless DC Motor Control

Powered by STM32G431RBT internal comparators, ADC, timers, interrupts, and PWM signals

Purpose and Function

Utilize an STM32 to create an ESC for a brushless DC motor and design a three phase inverter.

Once the available STM32 peripherals are determined, components are selected and an ESC design that efficiently utilizes these peripherals is made.

E.g. Feedback lines to measure back EMF to determine zero crossings, and IR2101 high and low side driver ICs that allow the STM32 to operate the power MOSFETS.

Code and Logic

To ensure reliable and effective commutation this Sensorless ESC utilizes an open loop start up mode, gradually building back EMF until it can be reliably measured. It then switches to closed loop mode and utilizes a delay equivalent to 30 electrical degrees before switching between commutation states.

Other features including dead time delay and using PWM complements are used to prevent MOSFET shoot through.

Example Code

void setphaseA(PHASE_STATE state, uint16_t duty) {

    switch (state) {
        case PHASE_PWM:
            //ENABLE REGISTER BITS FOR CH1 AND ITS COMPLEMENT
            //signal is output on the corresponding output pin
            TIM1->CCER |= TIM_CCER_CC1E;
            TIM1->CCER |= TIM_CCER_CC1NE;

            //GENERATE PWM WITH GIVEN DUTY CYCLE
            __HAL_TIM_SET_COMPARE(&htim1,TIM_CHANNEL_1,duty);

            break;

        case PHASE_LOW:
            //Pin for low side mosfet high, high side mosfet low
            TIM1->CCER |= TIM_CCER_CC1E;
            TIM1->CCER |= TIM_CCER_CC1NE;
            __HAL_TIM_SET_COMPARE(&htim1,TIM_CHANNEL_1,0);

            break;

        case PHASE_FLOAT:
            //Output disabled (not driven by the timer: High Impedance Hi-Z)
            TIM1->CCER &= ~TIM_CCER_CC1E;
            TIM1->CCER &= ~TIM_CCER_CC1NE;

            break;
    }
}
void HAL_COMP_TriggerCallback(COMP_HandleTypeDef *hcomp) {

    //Verify we are in Closed Loop Operation
    if (esc.mode != ESC_CLOSED_LOOP) {
        return;
    }

    //Make sure expected comparator has triggered interrupt
    if (hcomp != esc.expectedcomparator) {
        return;
    }

    //Save current time
    uint32_t currentVal = __HAL_TIM_GET_COUNTER(&htim2);
    //Find time between zero crossing (60 degrees)
    esc.electricalPeriod = currentVal - esc.lastZeroCross;
    esc.lastZeroCross = currentVal;
    //set commutation delay to 30 degrees
    esc.commutationdelay = esc.electricalPeriod/2;

    //Configure timer and set autoreload to trigger interrupt after 30 degree delay
    __HAL_TIM_SET_AUTORELOAD(&htim6, esc.commutationdelay);
    //Reset Counter
    __HAL_TIM_SET_COUNTER(&htim6, 0);
    //Start timer 6
    HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT(&htim6);
}

Result

Basic ESC for a brushless dc motor that allows control over motor speed. This project involved learning about brushless DC motor operation, writing firmware for the STM32, learning about PWM, ADCs, comparators, timers, and interrupts, as well as designing a three phase inverter.

Solar Power Supply

  • KiCad
  • Soldering
  • Circuit Design
  • Solar Power
  • Li-ion battery Charging
  • Solar Energy Harvesting

Includes External Solar Panel, USB-C, and LiPo Battery

Purpose and Function

Allow a small compact solar panel (~1-2W) or similar high impedance source to charge a 3.7V LiPo battery and power devices such as phones and low power devices such as microcontrollers.

After calculating component values a schematic with desired components is generated and footprints imported or created. Package type for components are also selected.

PCB Layout

Place PCB components, route traces, vias, and pours.

Utilize larger trace widths for power traces and where there are current and thermal performance requirements.

Avoid 90 angles in traces and utilize ground planes to minimize EMI effects and ensure manufacturability.

Manufacture

The result of this project is a solar power supply designed to allow high impedance sources to power low power and portable devices. The design is small, portable, and allows for a variety of power sources including solar panels.

Gerber files, Bill of Materials, and Component Placement List were generated for manufacturing.

Inverting Buck-Boost Converter

  • LTSpice
  • MATLAB
  • Circuit Design and Analysis
  • ESP32
  • ESP-IDF
  • VS Code

Includes custom high side MOSFET GATE driver and level shifter

Purpose and Function

Design a DC-DC converter that takes a variable input voltage (~3.5-20V) and outputs a constant -5V.

Utilize on-hand components and design additional circuits (such as a gate driver) so that the ESP32 PWM can be used.

Research similar devices on the market to decide tolerances and switching frequency.

Simulation and Design

Simulate the design in LTSpice and determine requirements of a gate driver that allow for a microcontroller to drive the gate of the MOSFET (i.e. level shifting and the implementation of a bootstrap capacitor).

Compare simulation to ideal behaviour modelling relationships such a duty cycle vs input voltage in MATLAB.

Design CharacteristicsCalculated Values
Switching Frequency 100 kHz, |Vout| = 5V, |Iout(max)| = 2AL = 100 µH, C = 220 µF

Result

The result of this project is an asynchronous inverting buck-boost converter that includes a totem pole high side MOSFET gate driver, level shifter, and bootstrap capacitor. The converter responds well to changes in PWM duty cycle and is capable of operating within a wide range of input voltages.

Example Improvements: Create a PCB for design and automatic duty cycle adjustment utilizing microcontroller ADC
